image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a pile of cooked Dungeness crabs. The crabs are stacked on top of each other, filling the frame. The shells exhibit characteristic reddish-brown and cream coloration with mottled patterns. Multiple claws and legs are visible, interlocking in a dense arrangement. The texture appears hard and calcified, consistent with cooked crustacean exoskeletons.

The mottling pattern on this specific shell appears slightly 'painted' or smeared compared to the sharper detail on others, lacking the natural micro-texture of a real exoskeleton.

The anatomy in the deep background becomes indistinct and logically ambiguous, with shapes that suggest crab parts but lack coherent structural definition, appearing as a textured blur rather than distinct objects.
